messages:
Maya G.: Quick Q — embeddings endpoint behavior for single-item batches with non-string input & unicode truncation. Repro: 
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-large","input":["€€€... (70k chars, mixed unicode)"]}'
```
Observed: for a one-item payload containing ~70k chars (multi-byte), the returned vector length was 1536 instead of the usual 768 and there was an HTTP header `x-embed-truncated: true`. Also saw `null` vectors when an item was an empty string inside a mixed batch. Is this expected/intentional? A bit worried about backward compat.

Alex R.: Short answer: that 1536 isn't expected for the canonical `redwood-embed-large` single-encoder path. Quick notes: we coerce non-string inputs via `String()` on the server (so numbers/booleans become strings). For hosted we truncate by UTF-8 byte length at 65,536 bytes (cut on codepoint boundary to avoid broken chars). The 1536 dim likely indicates routing to an ensemble/legacy encoder pair (two 768 outputs concatenated). That shouldn't happen for this model alias in normal cases.

Ryan T.: Context: last month we introduced an optional ensemble fallback for some long inputs; the alias resolution sometimes picks the ensemble under high load. There is a bug where single-item batches routed to the ensemble return concatenated vectors (1536). Empty-string -> `null` sounds like a marshalling edge: our marshaller returns `[]` for empty token sequences, and downstream JSON encoder sometimes serializes as `null` when type is ambiguous.

Maya G.: Thanks — couple asks: 1) Can we assert in the API contract that embeddings return shape [N, D] always and never switch dims per-request? 2) Document accepted input types (string, array-of-strings; other primitives coerced to string) and the truncation semantics (UTF-8 bytes, 65,536). 3) Guarantee no `null` vectors — either zero-vector or explicit error. 4) Add tests for single-item batches + mixed types + empty string behavior.

Sam P.: From product POV: if dim can change under certain routing, that's a breaking change for customers (we've seen clients assume fixed dim). Recommend we add an opt-in compatibility header `X-Embed-Compat: legacy` for customers who rely on old ensemble output, and default to stable single-dim behaviour. Also we should add a short customer-facing note if we change behavior.

Alex R.: I'll open a spec PR to make the contract explicit (input types, truncation policy, guaranteed output shape and dtype float32). I'll also add integration tests and a changelog entry. Ops: there's a routing fix to ensure alias resolution doesn't return ensemble for this model unless explicitly requested. @ci-bot can you run embedding tests on `fix/embed-routing` branch? :eyes:

ci-bot: CI triggered for branch `fix/embed-routing`. Running 42 embedding tests against staging image. Current results: 42 total, 2 failed — `test_single_item_ensemble_routing`, `test_empty_string_marshalling`. Logs: https://ci.redwood.local/builds/12345 (internal)

Ryan T.: I'll take the routing bug and the marshalling case. Plan: 1) Reject ensemble routing for aliases marked `stable-single-encoder` unless header `X-Embed-Mode: ensemble` is present. 2) Normalize empty-string outputs to zero-vector of length D (and include `x-embed-was-empty: true` header). 3) Add HTTP response metadata `vector_dim` and `truncated=true/false` in the JSON `meta` for easier client checks.

Maya G.: Great — please add the tests + PR links here when ready. Also add a one-paragraph blurb in the API spec page and mark it as required reading for SDKs. If anyone from SDKs wants to volunteer to bump client behavior for `null` -> zero-vector, please shout.

Alex R.: PR opened: https://git.redwood.infra/redwood/embeddings/pulls/678 (spec + tests). Ops ticket: RED-OPS-892 (routing), Product ticket: RED-PROD-412 (customer note & compat header).

Sam P.: I'll draft the customer note and send to legal/comms after we confirm the change window.

Maya G.: Thanks all — marking action items and will follow up in the PR. Closing thread when PR merges. :white_check_mark:
